target.title: Minoan Cryptanalysis: Computational Approaches to Deciphering Linear A and Assessing Its Connections with Language Families from the Mediterranean and the Black Sea Areas

stage_1_phonetic_grid_dependency.method: feature-based visual similarity comparison of Linear A signs with Cypriot Syllabary and Carian Alphabet signs
stage_1_phonetic_grid_dependency.importance_for_language_stage: The resulting provisional values populate the Linear A master-list New Format field used downstream.
stage_1_phonetic_grid_dependency.JANUS_interpretation: This stage is an upstream dependency and a source of researcher degrees of freedom; R3C-3 does not silently replace it with Linear B values.

stage_2_consonantal_comparison.comparison_input: one dictionary word list for the selected comparison language
stage_2_consonantal_comparison.matching_rule: exact equality between resulting consonant clusters
stage_2_consonantal_comparison.raw_output: all exact matches generated by the program
stage_2_consonantal_comparison.manual_filter_goal: retain matches judged more plausible and then compare meanings/context manually

author_stated_limitations_relevant_to_co: Published language matches are insufficient for a conclusive connection.
Match counts across compared languages are similar and some shared Linear A words match multiple languages, making coincidence a live explanation.
The feature set and manual visual filtering in the upstream phonetic-grid stage influence downstream results.
The Python program yields many matches and the displayed results are manually filtered.

epistemic_classification.reason_reproduction_blocked: Exact paper study inputs are not present in the JANUS registry; public repository identity alone does not establish byte-exact paper input identity.

next_gate: Freeze a corrective raw-match/permutation audit that cannot execute until exact input receipts pass.
